scenarios.requirement: A queue that fails on the loop tells its owner once, with CLOSED, after the queue is gone and between the loop's two hooks
An owner told once is not told again when its number is reused by a new pipe whose queue fails
A write refused at the call is the return value's: the owner of the descriptor is not told
A flush that fails returns the result, drops the queue, keeps the owner and tells nobody
Closing a descriptor forgets its owner, so a reused number never reaches the old owner
An owner is told after the walk of the writers: it may close another writer and reuse its number without meeting the walk
An owner is told before any reader is served: a reader closed or reopened on a reused number is not served with the old readiness
A number closed behind the loop tells its owner REFUSED and the loop closes nothing
A queue to a socket whose peer closed tells its owner once with CLOSED or REFUSED, whatever errno the system gives
With nothing else to wait for, an owed call makes the loop run it once and return at once
A wait counts the owed call as a source and asks its condition again after it
The loop does not sleep while a call is owed
An owe made inside the owed call is served by the next pass, once
The owed call is named once: a second, different call is refused
A queue the loop closes for its owner forgets the owner with the close
A failure owner is refused where it cannot be kept: a descriptor the loop closes, a negative number, no function, a full table
A queue handed to the loop to close has no owner when its number is lost
